clue.text: Lose weight ahead of surprisingly sturdy business opportunity

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly has not come out as expected, so the next word's letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: to lose weight is to grow thin
the letters of sturdy, rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter slims down before seizing a robust commercial chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of' places GROW THIN before the rearranged letters, giving GROWTH INDUSTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A growth industry is a sector expanding fast, so it is a promising field to invest or start up in.

clue.text: Having good taste is penalized again?

blocks.note: first meaning: cultivated and elegant
second meaning: read as ..., given a money penalty a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up split into RE and FINED.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means cultured and elegant, and split into a prefix plus a verb it means charged a penalty once more.

clue.text: Signaling young game?

blocks.note: whist is a card game
the suffix -ling marks a young one, as in duckling

explanation.surface: Giving a signal in a youngsters' game.
explanation.walkthrough: As a duckling is a young duck, a WHISTLING is read as a young whist; the question mark flags the made-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistling is a way of signaling, to a dog, a taxi or a team.

clue.text: That woman's in Germany with taxi containing red crustacean

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: her is the word for that woman
mit is the German word for with
a cab is a taxi
R is a standard abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: A woman in Germany rides a cab with a red lobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That woman's' is HER followed by ''s' meaning is; the C(R)AB goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit crab is a crustacean that lives in a borrowed shell.

clue.text: Points raising fashionable nonsense

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: in means fashionable
BS is a common slang abbreviation for nonsense

explanation.surface: Debate points that encourage trendy rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nibs are the writing points of pens, or small pointed tips generally.

clue.text: Florence leaves fish below

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they depart, so that short name is taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: Flo is the usual short form of Florence
a flounder is a flatfish

explanation.surface: Florence leaves fish in the water underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove FLO from the front of FLOUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Under and below are synonyms, both meaning in a lower position.

clue.text: Butler gets nothing after treatment for pains

indicators.note: something put through treatment is processed and altered, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A manservant gets no relief from medical treatment for his aches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pains' is the noun as in 'taking pains', the effort or bother something costs.
explanation.definitionFit: To take pains is to take trouble, so the two nouns share the sense of effort and bother.

clue.text: Nation's desire to imprison me

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock inside, so the last word goes within the other

blocks.note: a yen is a longing or desire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country wants to lock me up.
explanation.walkthrough: YE(ME)N. Nation is also this magazine's name, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a country on the Arabian peninsula, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Triangle reconfiguration is a key concept in calculus

indicators.note: a reconfiguration sets the parts up in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rearranging a triangle is central to a mathematics course.
explanation.definitionFit: The integral, the area under a curve, is one of the two fundamental ideas of calculus alongside the derivative.

clue.text: "Flipper Returns": story is comparatively cool

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word before it is read from the end

blocks.note: a flipper is a fin, as on a dolphin
a story of a building is a level or tier

explanation.surface: A sequel to the dolphin TV show Flipper is judged hipper than the original.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks dress it as a film title; really it is an instruction. Story is the American spelling of storey, a floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is slang for smart or stylish, so its comparative form describes something cooler than another.

clue.text: Terrible boredom in the boudoir

indicators.note: a terrible version is badly made, so the following word's letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is dreadfully bored in a lady's private room.
explanation.definitionFit: A boudoir is a woman's private sitting room or bedchamber, an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Confused nineties scientist

indicators.note: confused things are muddled up, so the next word's letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A researcher bewildered by the 1990s, or perhaps by old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein is the most famous physicist of the twentieth century, an example of the category.

clue.text: Letters from Doug, Rob and Josh

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken straight from the run of words that follows, in order

blocks.note: a run of letters across the end of Doug, all of Rob and the start of and

explanation.surface: Correspondence from three men named Doug, Rob and Josh.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh looks like the third name in a list; it is the definition, a first name whose surname is hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Josh Groban is an American singer, so his surname is clued by his first name.

clue.text: Grand, ancient head of government took in a California landmark

indicators.note: 'head of' keeps only the first letter of 'government'

blocks.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand dollars
olden means of long ago
the head, or first letter, of government
to take in food is to eat it

explanation.surface: A grand old leader once welcomed a famous Californian site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took in' looks like a container signal but here means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco is the state's best-known landmark.

clue.text: After failed raid, incomplete lines coming from the center

indicators.note: a failed attempt has fallen apart, so the word it describes is broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters of raid, rearranged
the word is left incomplete, only its first letter kept

explanation.surface: After an unsuccessful raid, lines of battle are left broken, retreating from the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the rearranged raid first; 'incomplete' cuts itself down to its own first letter, which is the loosest step here.
explanation.definitionFit: Radii are the plural of radius, straight segments running from a circle's middle out to its edge.

clue.text: Uses a hook to keep time for musical notes

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: someone who uses a hook to make lace or yarn work crochets
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A knitter's hookwork keeps rhythm for a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: Crotchet is the British name for a quarter note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is the British term for a quarter note, one beat in common time.

clue.text: Commuter to complain about bathroom on the way back

indicators.note: going on the way back means heading in the opposite direction, so these words read backwards

blocks.note: to carp is to complain
re means about, as in a memo
loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles about needing the toilet on the journey home.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for a toilet; the reversal takes both 'about' and 'bathroom' together, so their order flips too.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpooler shares car journeys to work with others, a kind of commuter.

clue.text: Doctor Seuss to grab a writing implement? That makes you nervous

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the name's letters get rearranged
to grab is to seize and hold, so the writing tool ends up inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: The children's author Dr. Seuss reaches for a pen, which is nerve-racking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Seuss' reads as the author's name, but Doctor is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious tension of waiting to learn what happens, which is what makes you nervous.

clue.text: Summer employee changes gear fluid

indicators.note: the following words are changed around, their letters reordered into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A seasonal worker at a garage swaps out the transmission fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes gear fluid' reads as car maintenance; 'changes' is the signal and gear fluid the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeguards are typically hired for the summer season to watch swimmers at pools and beaches.

clue.text: Piece of music with peanuts and crackerjack?

blocks.note: first meaning: a brief flourish of trumpets
second meaning: the snacks a sports fan eats at a baseball game

explanation.walkthrough: Peanuts and Cracker Jack (caramel popcorn) are the snacks in 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game'; the question mark admits the split into FAN FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short ceremonial tune for trumpets, and split in two it means the food fans eat.

clue.text: Confederate soldier: American puzzle

blocks.note: a Reb (rebel) was a soldier of the Confederacy in the US Civil War
US is short for American, as in the US flag

explanation.surface: A Civil War Confederate soldier poses an American puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle that represents words with pictures, symbols or letters.

clue.text: BA gives you something to put around your neck

definitions.text: something to put around your neck

blocks.note: the pair of letters B, A, described in words

explanation.surface: A Bachelor of Arts degree earns you a scarf, or a British Airways gift.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the two letters aloud as a description: B AND AN A, which runs together as BANDANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large printed handkerchief often tied around the neck or head.

clue.text: Type of hit!

blocks.note: surface reading: a kind of blow or punch
setter's reading: a baseball hit that gets the batter to first base, and also a hit record released on its own

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints the word works two ways: a baseball hit reaching first base, and a pop record that charts.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the most basic base hit is one base, and a chart hit is usually a song released by itself.

clue.text: Small, tough fragment

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
hard means tough

explanation.surface: A little piece of something hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken piece of glass or pottery.

clue.text: Adds a substance to something needed to bring back house calls

indicators.note: something from the following words means only a part of them is wanted
bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the part is read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the end of house and the start of calls

explanation.surface: A drug is slipped into the bag a doctor needs to revive the practice of home visits.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of house and first of calls, read backwards, give LACES.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace a drink is to spike it with alcohol or a drug, adding a substance to it.

clue.text: Advertise a lightweight on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so what is wanted is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: an ounce is a light unit of weight

explanation.surface: Promote a featherweight boxer in a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is about 28 grams.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something publicly known, close in sense to promoting it.

clue.text: Child heard flying toy's return

indicators.note: heard means the wordplay works on sounds, not on spelling
a return goes back the other way, so the sounds are run backwards

blocks.note: a kite is a flying toy; its sounds K, long I, T said in reverse order

explanation.surface: A child hears his kite come back down.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal is of sounds, not letters: kite is said k-eye-t, and backwards that is t-eye-k.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyke is an informal word for a small child, often a mischievous one.

clue.text: Symbol of St. Louis, surrounded by some chaos

indicators.note: something surrounded by another is enclosed within it, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: some and any are interchangeable, as in 'got any?'
the Gateway Arch is the landmark of St. Louis, Missouri

explanation.surface: The St. Louis landmark is engulfed in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a quantity word; here it is the outer piece, since some and any are interchangeable in questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawless disorder, a close synonym for complete chaos.

clue.text: FRANKEN CLAPS, GOES CRAZY?

indicators.note: a word that goes crazy loses its order, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: Al Franken, the comedian and former US senator
the letters of claps, rearranged

explanation.surface: Senator Franken applauds and goes wild, shouting.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is printed in capitals, which is what the answer names; typing in capitals reads as shouting, matching the crazy applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Text set entirely in capital letters, like this clue, is said to be in that style, often read as yelling.

clue.text: Heralds providing necessary contributions for dry run

indicators.note: the first word provides the stock of letters, to be drawn on in any order and as often as the answer requires

blocks.note: the word supplies the stock of letters, each used once here
the further copies of letters from that same stock that the answer needs

explanation.surface: Messengers chip in what is needed for a practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter-bank clue: every letter of the answer is one of H, E, R, A, L, D, S, and those seven letters, reused as necessary, spell all fourteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A dress rehearsal is the final full run-through before opening night, a trial performance in costume.
